Re:     Wolverine Power Supply Cooperative, Inc., Docket No. ER27-___-000
        Request for Change in Rates to Distribution Cooperative Member-Owners

 Dear Secretary Reese:

         Pursuant to Section 205 of the Federal Power Act (“FPA”), 1 and Section 35.13 of the
 regulations of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or the “Commission”), 2
 Wolverine Power Supply Cooperative, Inc. (“Wolverine”) hereby submits a superseding cost-of
 service rate schedule (the “Rate Filing”). The Rate Filing amends Wolverine’s existing FERC Rate
 Schedule No. 4, which establishes the wholesale requirements cost-of-service rates charged to
 Wolverine’s six distribution cooperative member-owners: Cherryland Electric Cooperative, Great
 Lakes Energy Cooperative, HomeWorks Tri-County Electric Cooperative, Midwest Energy &
 Communications, Presque Isle Electric & Gas Co-op, and Thumb Electric Cooperative (each a
 “Distribution Member” and collectively the “Distribution Members”). These rates are charged
 pursuant to a separate wholesale power contract between Wolverine and each Distribution
 Member. 3

        Wolverine is governed by its Board of Directors consisting of two representatives from
 each Distribution Member, which sets the strategic direction of the cooperative, oversees policies,
 and generally guides operations. As evidenced by the Board of Directors Resolution included as
 Attachment C hereto, the Rate Filing is unanimously supported by Wolverine’s Directors, whom
 are nominated by all six Distribution Members and the only customers affected by the Rate Filing.
 Therefore, Wolverine requests that the Commission approve the Rate Filing without suspension,
 hearing, or condition.


 1
   16 U.S.C. § 824d (2018).
 2
   18 C.F.R. § 35.13 (2020).
 3
   Wolverine Power Supply Cooperative, Inc., Docket No. ER20-1206-000 (letter order issued May 5, 2020);
 Wolverine Power Supply Cooperative, Inc., Docket No. ER25-265-000 (letter order issued December 16,
 2024).
 Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Secretary
October 1, 2026

         Wolverine requests an effective date for the Rate Filing of January 1, 2027. Wolverine
 further requests that the Commission issue an order accepting the Rate Filing as expeditiously as
 possible, but in any event no later than December 1, 2026. A ruling by December 1, 2026, will
 provide Wolverine personnel sufficient time to prepare its billing system, update the Distribution
 Members, and generally provide for a seamless implementation of the revenue-neutral Rate
 Stabilization Rider for the first billing cycle in January 2027.


 I.        BACKGROUND

        Wolverine is a Michigan-based not-for-profit generation and transmission electric
 cooperative that provides wholesale service to its eight members and is subject to the
 Commission’s jurisdiction under the FPA. Wolverine’s six Distribution Members purchase both
 generation and transmission service from Wolverine and resell that power at retail to
 approximately 300,000 service locations (“member consumers”), primarily in Michigan’s Lower
 Peninsula. Wolverine’s two other member-owners are Wolverine Power Marketing Cooperative,
 Inc. (“WPMC”), a Michigan Public Service Commission-license Alternative Electric Supplier in
 Michigan and Spartan Renewable Energy, Inc. (“Spartan”), a specialty member based in
 Michigan. 4 Wolverine’s members are both its customers and its owners.

        Wolverine is a Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc. (“MISO”) Transmission
 Owner with a transmission system consisting of approximately 1,600 miles of 69 kV and 138 kV
 looped transmission lines and associated facilities. These transmission facilities are included in the
 Michigan Joint Zone under MISO’s Open Access Transmission, Energy and Operating Reserve
 Markets Tariff. Wolverine is an active participant in organized power markets administered by
 MISO and the PJM Interconnection (“PJM”).


 II.       DESCRIPTION OF FILING

           A.          Existing Rate Design

         Wolverine’s existing wholesale requirements rates were accepted most recently in Docket
 No. ER21-66-000. As a not-for-profit entity, Wolverine’s rates are designed to provide its
 Distribution Members with wholesale rates that allow them to offer competitively-priced power to
 their existing and prospective retail member-consumers, while, at the same time, allowing for full
 recovery of Wolverine’s cost of service to support forecasted business activities, including a target
 margin component that ensures Wolverine’s financial ratios exceed the financial covenants in its
 loan agreements within a range of reasonableness established by Wolverine. Collectively,
 Wolverine’s rate design aligns with cost-causation principles by allocating fixed costs of


 4
   Wolverine engages in power sales to WPMC and Spartan separately under Wolverine’s market-based rate
 tariff. Accordingly, this Rate Filing does not affect WPMC or Spartan.

 Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Secretary
October 1, 2026
Page 3 of 7


 generation consistent with the incurrence of cost, unbundling energy costs, and sending
 appropriate price signals for Distribution Member load control.

         Wolverine’s existing rate structure consists of formula rate components to recover
 Wolverine’s fixed and variable costs that are designed to collect required revenues based on
 Wolverine’s forecasted cost of service for the upcoming calendar year with a true-up mechanism
 to ensure that only actual costs are collected. The formula rates recover Wolverine costs of service
 based on general cost causation, specifically related to demand and energy components. These
 costs of service components are reduced accordingly when actual revenues from non-member
 sources (“External Revenues”) are received, including revenues associated with Wolverine’s
 participation in MISO and PJM.

         Wolverine’s present rate design was developed collaboratively with the Distribution
 Members to be clear, flexible, and fair to all Distribution Members while accommodating load
 growth and enhancing flexibility to accommodate unique member-consumer electrical demands.
 Importantly, Wolverine’s rate structure accommodates the desire of the Distribution Members for
 stabilized costs. As noted, Wolverine’s rate structure is formulaic and includes a mechanism to
 true-up fixed costs from the prior year budget, margin, and return of fixed revenue credit associated
 with capacity sales to ensure an appropriate level of cost recovery.

           B.          Change in Rates

        This filing amends Rate Schedule No. 4 in three ways: (1) adopting a “Rate Stabilization
 Rider;” (2) adopting a cap to the eligibility for the Commercial and Industrial (“C&I”) rate; and
 (3) miscellaneous editorial clean-up, including removing the now obsolete True-Up Rider. 5

                       1.    Rate Stabilization Rider

         Current market conditions are driving significant volatility in External Revenue that
 directly and immediately reduces (or in a year with little to no External Revenue, increases)
 Distribution Member rates on a short-term basis. Specifically, in recent years, wholesale energy
 market prices in the MISO and PJM regions have experienced significant volatility driven by
 fluctuating natural gas prices, variable renewable energy output, and shifting capacity market
 dynamics, resulting in External Revenues that have varied materially from year to year,
 underscoring the need for a rate mechanism that smooths these fluctuations rather than passing
 them through directly and immediately to Distribution Members – causing direct and immediate
 rate unpredictability. The proposed “Rate Stabilization Rider” will allow Wolverine to provide
 better rate predictability, sustain its wholesale rate competitiveness, and enhance long-term
 financial flexibility.



 5
  The True-up Rider was included in the current Rate Schedule to transition from the prior Rate Schedule
 and is no longer applicable.




4922-5736-9291, v. 5
 Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Secretary
October 1, 2026
Page 4 of 7


             The Rate Stabilization Rider, which was developed in consultation with all Distribution
    Members and adopted unanimously, is designed to be revenue-neutral with a goal to provide
    predictability and stability, competitiveness, and flexibility for the long-term. The addition of the
    Rate Stabilization Rider does not collect or require any additional revenue from Distribution
    Members. The only sources of additional revenue remain external as contemplated under the
    current rate (e.g., MISO Market revenue from energy sales from Wolverine’s natural gas peaking
    fleet, bilateral sales to non-member electric providers, etc.). The Rate Stabilization Rider changes
    only the timing or manner that those External Revenues are utilized for the benefit of Distribution
    Members.

            Mechanically, the Rate Stabilization Rider allows Wolverine’s Board of Directors to
    establish an annual rate target to provide: (1) predictability as Wolverine will bill its Distribution
    Members exactly to the target or the lowest achievable rate depending on External Revenues; and
    (2) competitiveness by setting a target to align with recent historical rates. Once the target is
    achieved, any External Revenues that remain are automatically deferred to achieve a future
    monthly or annual rate target furthering the predictability and competitiveness objectives. Finally,
    if Wolverine’s Board determines that the deferred revenue balance (i.e., the Rate Stabilization
    Fund) reaches a satisfactory level, it may elect to, via new Board Resolution, recognize a portion
    of the deferred revenue as margin to enhance long-term financial flexibility for Wolverine and its
    Distribution Members and/or make patronage capital retirements back to the Distribution
    Members.

             The Rate Stabilization Rider is consistent with the Commission’s long-established
    regulatory framework for automatic adjustment clauses, which permits utilities to adjust rates to
    reflect fluctuations in fuel and purchased power costs. 6

                       2.   C&I Rate

            The current C&I Rate is available to any Distribution Member for eligible member-
    consumer load of at least 1 MW. However, as the risks associated with servicing large loads
    increase, the Distribution Members have adopted or are working to limit the size of eligible load
    under their retail tariffs. Exceptionally large C&I loads (e.g., above 15 MW) present
    disproportionate cost-allocation and reliability risks to the remaining member-consumers. The
    departure or significant load reduction of a single very large customer could cause abrupt cost
    shifts to the remaining customer base, undermining rate stability for the cooperative as a whole.



6
  See also, Tri-State Generation and Transmission Association, Inc., 170 FERC ¶ 61,223 at P 13, 54 (2020)
(accepting bylaws that requires the utility to account on a patronage basis to all its members for all amounts
received and receivable from the furnishing of electric power and energy, including, among other items,
adjustments to reserves or deferred credit accounts for the purpose of stabilizing margins and rate increases
from year to year).




4922-5736-9291, v. 5
 Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Secretary
October 1, 2026
Page 5 of 7


 Consequently, Wolverine is amending its C&I Rate to adopt a 15 MW cap on eligibility.7 Aligning
 Wolverine’s wholesale eligibility cap with the retail-level caps already adopted or being adopted
 by most Distribution Members ensures consistency across the wholesale and retail tariff structures.

                       3.    Miscellaneous Clean-Up

         Finally, Wolverine is revising Rate Schedule No. 4 to correct miscellaneous grammatical
 errors or other minor editorial edits, including removing the now obsolete True-Up Rider, none of
 which will have any rate impact.


 III.      COMPLIANCE WITH 18 C.F.R. § 35.13

         The Rate Stabilization Rider is designed to be revenue-neutral, as it is not dependent on
 any additional revenue from Wolverine’s Distribution Members. Importantly, in no scenario will
 any Distribution Member be charged more than its actual cost of service under the existing rate
 structure. Accordingly, this Rate Filing qualifies under the abbreviated filing requirements of 18
 C.F.R. § 35.13(a)(2)(iii).

        In compliance with the requirements of 18 C.F.R. § 35.13, Wolverine submits the
 following:

           A.          List of Documents Submitted – Section 35.13(b)(1)

                1. This transmittal letter;

                2. Revised Rate Schedule No. 4 (Attachment A); 8

                3. Redline Comparison (Attachment B);

                4. Wolverine Board of Directors Resolution approving and authorizing the
                   submission of the Rate Filing (Attachment C); and

                5. Certificate of Service and List of Persons Served (Attachment D).

           B.          Proposed Effective Date of the Rate Change – Section 35.13(b)(2)

           As discussed, Wolverine requests an effective date of January 1, 2027.




 7
   Loads above 15 MW would be supplied under alternative arrangements separate and apart from the C&I
 Rate (e.g., bilateral contracts under Wolverine’s MBR authority).
 8
   Rate Schedule No. 4 is also submitted in eTariff format.

October 1, 2026

           C.          Names and Addresses of Persons to Whom a Copy of the Rate Schedule
                       Change Has Been Served – Section 35.13(b)(3)

           Wolverine has served each of its Distribution Members with a copy of the Rate Filing.

           D.          Brief Description of the Rate Schedule Change – Section 35.13(b)(4)

           A brief description of the proposed rate schedule change is provided in this transmittal
 letter.

           E.          Statement of the Reasons for the Rate Schedule Change – Section
                       35.13(b)(5)

        A brief description of the reasons for the proposed rate schedule change is provided in this
 transmittal letter.

           F.          Showing That All Requisite Agreement to the Rate Schedule Change,
                       or to the Filing of the Rate Schedule Change, Has Been Obtained –
                       Section 35.13(b)(6)

         No agreement is required for Commission approval of the rate schedule change, or the
 filing of the rate schedule change with the Commission. Nonetheless, as noted above, Wolverine
 has obtained unanimous support from its Board of Directors for the Rate Filing.

           G.          Statement Governing Inclusion of Any Expenses or Costs in Cost-of-
                       Service Statements That Have Been Alleged or Adjudged Illegal,
                       Duplicative, or Unnecessary Costs That Are Demonstrably the Product
                       of Discriminatory Employment Practices – Section 35.13(b)(7)

        Wolverine is not submitting cost of service statements for Period I or Period II with this
 abbreviated Rate Filing. Nonetheless, none of Wolverine’s expenses or costs have been alleged or
 adjudged to be illegal, duplicative, or unnecessary and demonstrably the product of discriminatory
 employment practices.

                                           Definitions

As used in this Rate Schedule No. 4, the following terms have the meanings specified below:

Actual Cost – the cost recorded by Wolverine after the receipt of an invoice during the Rate
Year (N) that is reported on its FERC Form 1.

Actual Revenue – the revenue received and recorded by Wolverine after issuance of an invoice
during the Rate Year (N) that is reported on its FERC Form 1.

Ancillary Services – services that are necessary to support Capacity and the transmission of
Energy from resources to delivery points while maintaining reliable operation of the transmission
system in accordance with Good Utility Practice.

Annual Budget – Wolverine’s projection produced no later than September 30 prior to the
immediately upcoming Rate Year (N) of all Direct Fixed Costs, Indirect Fixed Costs, Fixed
Revenue Credits, to be recovered and provided during the Rate Year (N).

Annual Budget True-up – the mechanism to return or collect from the D Members the actual
Fixed Cost or Fixed Revenue Credit variance from the Annual Budget. Examples include
unexpected repairs, increased maintenance expense, or decreases in operating costs from those
included in the Annual Budget.

Annual Coincident Peak – the highest single hourly Demand Metered during a given calendar
year for all D Members, expressed in MW.

Annual Demand Response Resource (ADRR) – Demand Response Resource capable of
performing every month of the year.

Annual Energy Sales – the total amount of Energy Metered during a given calendar year for all
D Members, expressed in MWh.

Annual Forecast – Wolverine’s projection produced no later than September 30 prior to the
immediately upcoming Rate Year (N) of all Variable Costs and Variable Revenue to be
recovered and provided during the Rate Year (N).

Annual Peak Capacity Resource (APCR) – a resource capable of meeting or reducing Metered
Load however, seasonal availability, performance capability, or efficiency limits regular output
to fewer than 12 months per year. For units fired by fossil fuel this category shall include those
units with heat rates of 12,000 BTU/kWh and higher. SDRR are included in this category.




4938-9272-6739, v. 1
 Wolverine Power Supply Cooperative, Inc.                                             Page 3 of 40
Rate Schedule No. 4, Version 5.0.0


Annual Peak Fixed Costs – the total Direct Fixed Costs for all Resources that meet the criteria
of an APCR.

Annual Peak Resource Energy Credit – Variable Revenues received from Energy sales minus
Variable Cost incurred in the production of Energy by Resources whose costs are recovered in
the Annual Peak Fixed Costs.

Base Resource Energy Credit – Variable Revenue from Energy sales minus Variable Cost
incurred in the production of Energy by Resources whose costs are recovered in Base Fixed
Costs.

Baseload Resource – a resource that generally is operating at a minimum level of output (MW)
most days each year to maintain mechanical availability and support system demand. This
includes all coal-fired resources, nuclear resources, and combined-cycle natural gas resources
with heat rates less than 7,999 BTU/kWh.

Base Fixed Costs – the total annual Direct Fixed Cost for all resources that are included in the
Baseload Resource category, Wolverine-owned Renewable Resources, and all other owned
resources not captured in APCR or MPCR categories, all Indirect Fixed Costs to be billed
throughout the applicable rate year (N), represented in dollars.

Billing Month – the month for which the current bill is being issued. For example, January’s bill
is based on December results; therefore, December is the referenced Billing Month.

Capacity – the maximum ability to produce or avoid the consumption of electricity, generally
expressed in MW. For the purpose of this rate schedule, it is generally used to represent that
which can be sold or utilized within the RTO, as required to meet Demand obligations with
generation or Demand Response resources.

C&I – commercial and industrial Member-Consumers receiving retail electric service from D
members and billed from Wolverine under the C&I Rate.

C&I Maximum Demand – the C&I Member-Consumer’s highest hourly Metered Demand
during the previous three completed Rate Years (N-2, N-3, N-4).

Commercial Fiber – supplemental fiber optic cables installed with Wolverine’s Utility Fiber
available to enable non-Wolverine utility purpose or other non-utility communications purpose,
included as part of Wolverine’s Shared Excluded Facilities.

 Wolverine Power Supply Cooperative, Inc.                                                  Page 4 of 40

Committed Fixed Costs – costs that are unavoidable as Wolverine is obligated by ownership or
contract to pay regardless of Wolverine operations, D Member Load, or dispatch of the asset.
Committed Fixed Costs include, but are not limited to, interest, depreciation, property tax, and
Capacity PPAs.

Committed Variable Costs –costs that are unavoidable as Wolverine is obligated, by ownership
or contract, to pay regardless of Wolverine operations, D Member Load, or performance of the
obligation. Committed Variable Costs include, but are not limited to; Energy PPAs, including
renewables, fuel, and fuel transportation.

Current Month – the month in which the bill is being issued. For example, if December is the
Billing Month, January is generally the month in which the bill is issued – January is the Current
Month.

Day-Ahead Locational Marginal Pricing (DA LMP) – an inclusive price for Energy,
congestion, and losses calculated for each hour one day in advance of delivery for a specific
commercial pricing node within a given RTO and represented in $/MWh.

Demand – the maximum integrated hourly sum of Load occurring over a specified period, such
as an hour, day, month, season, or year, expressed in MWs.

Demand Response – the ability to reduce Demand via distributed generation or command of
other distributed devices on the distribution system.

Demand Response Credit – reduction in the monthly bill provided to the D Member for the
ability of the D Member to control and reduce Demand via D Member Demand Response,
qualifications further described herein.

Direct Fixed Costs – costs associated with investing, maintaining, and owning Wolverine’s
power plants, transmission facilities, distribution substations, or other facilities for the benefit of
D Members. These costs include, but are not limited to, depreciation, interest, property tax,
personnel (labor and benefits), and regular and on-going operations and maintenance expense.
For the avoidance of doubt, these costs may be incurred by Wolverine as Demand costs (or
similar naming convention) for jointly owned facilities, PPAs, or other direct power plant
purchase arrangements that pass-through fixed costs directly and specifically associated with a
unit(s).

D Members –Wolverine’s Distribution Cooperative Member-Owners.

D Member Annual Peak Cost Share –proportion of the Individual D Member Average Annual
Coincident Peak, including SDRR add-back, divided by Total Average Annual Coincident Peak.

D Member Base Fixed Cost Share –proportion of the Individual D Member Average Energy
Sales divided by Total D Member Average Energy Sales.

D Member Monthly Peak Cost Share –proportion of the Individual D Member Average
Monthly Coincident Peak, including ADRR add-back, divided by Total Average D Member
Monthly Coincident Peak.

Distribution Cooperative Member-Owners –the distribution cooperative member-owners that
purchase generation and transmission service from Wolverine pursuant to a Wholesale Power
Contract.

Dynamic Energy Cost – the hourly composite average of Energy-Weighted DA LMP at all
commercial pricing nodes at which Wolverine delivers Energy to its D Members.

EPT – Eastern Prevailing Time and is either Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Savings
Time, whichever is in effect in Cadillac, MI on the relevant date and hour.

Energy – an amount of electricity that is produced, purchased, consumed, sold, or transmitted
over a period of time and measured or calculated in MWh.

Energy Stabilization Cost – if positive, the amount charged, or, if negative, credited, to D
Members determined by subtracting the cost of Wolverine’s PPA commitments from the DA
LMP or RT LMP at the respective commercial pricing node at which each PPA is settled, as
determined in the respective contract or confirmation. Wolverine’s PPA Commitments, as
described herein, excludes forward renewable contracts, as those commitments are recovered via
Renewable Energy Cost mechanism.

Energy-Weighted DA LMP –the product of hourly Metered Energy sales and the hourly DA
LMP at each of the nodes that Wolverine serves the D Members.

Estimated Cost – throughout the Rate Year (N) Wolverine shall recover costs based on the best
available data at the time of billing. Since this data is not final, it is subject to change; therefore,
these costs are subject to True-up as further described herein.

Estimated Revenue Credits – throughout the Rate Year (N) Wolverine shall distribute credits
based on the best available data at the time of billing. Since this data is not final, it is subject to
change; therefore, these revenues are subject to True-up as further described herein.

FERC – Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, and any successor agency.

Fixed Cost Distribution – proportion determined by dividing the total D Member Billing
Month’s 3-year average Metered Energy sales from the three previously completed Rate Years
(N-2, N-3, N-4) by the total D Member annual 3-year average Metered Energy sales from the
three previously completed Rate Years (N-2, N-3, N-4).

Fixed Revenue – revenue received for sales of Capacity and Ancillary Services, as defined by
RTOs, including but not limited to Voltage and Reactive Support, to any non-D Member or via
MBR contract to D Member.

Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) – a common set of accounting principles,
standards, and procedures issued by the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB).

Good Utility Practice – any of the practices, methods and acts engaged in or approved by a
significant portion of the electric utility industry during the relevant time period, or any of the
practices, methods and acts which, in the exercise of reasonable judgment in light of the facts
known at the time the decision is made, could have been expected to accomplish the desired
result at a reasonable cost consistent with good business practices, reliability, safety and
expedition. Good Utility Practice is not intended to be limited to the optimum practice, method,
or act to the exclusion of all others, but rather, intended to include acceptable practices, methods,
or acts generally accepted in the region, including those practices required by Federal Power Act
Section 215(a)(4).

Gross Book Value – the total value of an asset as recorded in Wolverine’s accounting records,
as determined in accordance with Uniform System of Accounts and prior to depreciation.

Indirect Fixed Costs – costs, such as administrative and general costs, associated with investing
in, maintaining, and owning and operating Wolverine’s business functions. These costs include,
but are not limited to; depreciation, interest, and property tax related to general plant, personnel
(labor and benefits), and regular and on-going operations and maintenance expenses for
Wolverine to maintain its on-going business functions.

Individual D Member Average Annual Coincident Peak – the sum of the individual D
Member’s Metered Non-C&I Demand at the Non-C&I Annual Coincident Peak from the three
previously completed Rate Years (N-2, N-3, N-4) divided by three (3).

Individual D Member Average Energy Sales – the sum of the Metered Annual Energy Sales to
the individual D Member from the three previously completed Rate Years (N-2, N-3, N-4)
divided by three (3).

Individual D Member Average Monthly Coincident Peak – the sum of the individual D
Member’s Metered Demand at the Monthly Coincident Peak from every month during the three
previously completed Rate Years (N-2, N-3, N-4) divided by thirty-six (36).

kW – kilowatt.

kWh – kilowatt-hour.

Load – the amount of Energy (MWh) consumed by such D Member.

MISO – Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc., or successor RTO.

MW – megawatt.

MWh – megawatt-hour.

Margin – the amount of revenue collected over and above Wolverine costs.

Market Based Rate (MBR) Sales – sales by Wolverine of Energy, Capacity, and market
services to D Members, other Wolverine members, and wholesale customers, on a contractual
basis utilizing its FERC-approved Market Based Rate Authority.

Member-Consumer(s) – the retail customer(s) of a D Member.

Member Directed Resource (MDR) – generating units, battery systems, or other devices that
are capable of producing or reducing consumption that Wolverine either constructs or contracts
at the specific direction of one or more D Member, but not all D Members, subject to the
qualifications and limitations further described herein.

Meter – the measurement device to determine the Load and Demand for the locations that
Wolverine serves Load. Generally, the meter is located on the high side of the distribution
transformer or, if on the low side, adjusted to reflect the transformer losses. In the case of
Resources, it shall be determined by the location of the measurement device at or near the
respective resource and the number reported will be adjusted for applicable transformation and
distribution losses.

Rate Schedule No. 4, Version 5.0.0


Monthly Coincident Peak – the highest single hourly Demand Metered in a given month for all
D Members measured concurrently, expressed in MW.

Monthly Peak Capacity Resource (MPCR) – a resource capable of meeting or reducing
Demand with regular availability during every month of the year, January through December.
For units fired by fossil fuel this category shall include those units with heat rates between 8,000
BTU/kWh and 11,999 BTU/kWh. Additionally, Capacity PPAs for all non-Baseload and ADRR
resources shall be included in this category.

Monthly Peak Fixed Costs – the total annual Direct Fixed Costs for all resources that are
included in the MPCR category.

MPCR Energy Credit – Variable Revenue from the Metered Energy sales minus Variable Cost
incurred in the production of Energy by Resources whose costs are recovered in Monthly Peak
Fixed Costs.

N – represents a particular calendar year for which the rate is effective.

         2. Wolverine’s highest incremental cost of any generation or purchases of power during
            all hours served, plus ten (10) percent, plus applicable transmission Costs and
            ancillary service Costs; and
         3. The highest locational marginal price applicable to Wolverine for all hours served,
            plus ten (10) percent, plus applicable transmission Costs and ancillary service Costs.

Standby Fixed Cost

The Standby Fixed Cost shall be the hourly average, expressed in $/MWh, of all Wolverine’s
Fixed Costs, plus ten (10) percent, for the highest single hourly Metered Demand of the
Member-Consumer during the entire period the standby service was required.




4938-9272-6739, v. 1
 Wolverine Power Supply Cooperative, Inc.                                           Page 39 of 40
Rate Schedule No. 4, Version 5.0.0


                                   Rate Stabilization Rider


Rate Target

Beginning with Rate Year, 2027, and for each Rate Year thereafter, Wolverine shall set a Rate
Target for its Total Power Supply and Delivery Rate. For Rate Year 2027 the Rate Target is
established by the Wolverine Board of Directors in accordance with the Resolution authorizing
this Rate Stabilization Rider. For each subsequent Rate Year, starting with Rate Year 2028, the
Wolverine Board of Directors shall establish the Rate Target to align with the Annual Forecast
deadline.

Total Power Supply and Delivery Rate shall be defined as Wolverine’s total cost of energy,
capacity, and power delivery to supply its D Members under this Rate Schedule. Total Power
Supply Rate is calculated as follows:

Total Power Supply and Delivery Rate ($/MWh) = [Fixed Cost Charges and Revenue Credits +
Variable Costs and Revenues] / Annual Energy Sales for the applicable Rate Year

Rate Stabilization Fund

At the end of each Billing Month Wolverine shall manage its Total Power Supply and Delivery
Rate to achieve the Rate Target. The Rate Stabilization Fund shall be established to achieve the
Rate Target for the benefit of D Members. At the end of each Billing Month, Wolverine shall
determine whether the funds will be deposited to or withdrawn from the Rate Stabilization Fund
as follows:

Rate Stabilization Fund Deposit/(Withdrawal) ($) = [Rate Target ($/MWh) – Total Power Supply
and Delivery Rate ($/MWh) for the applicable Billing Month] * Energy Sales for the applicable
Billing Month

If the results of the calculation above are positive, the amount shall be deposited as a Rate
Stabilization Fund Deposit and held for future use by Wolverine to achieve the Rate Target or for
other purposes as defined herein.

If the results of the calculation above are negative, the amount shall be withdrawn as a Rate
Stabilization Fund Withdrawal to be applied as Variable Revenue, to achieve the Rate Target.

Insufficient Stabilization Fund Balance

If a Rate Stabilization Fund Withdrawal is required because the Rate Target was not achieved
and the then-current balance of the fund is insufficient to achieve the Rate Target, the




4938-9272-6739, v. 1
 Wolverine Power Supply Cooperative, Inc.                                        Page 40 of 40
Rate Schedule No. 4, Version 5.0.0


Stabilization Fund Withdrawal shall be drawn to zero to reduce the Total Power Supply and
Delivery Rate as close to the Target Rate as possible.

Other Withdrawals

At the discretion of the Wolverine Board of Directors, funds may be withdrawn from the Rate
Stabilization Fund for power supply investment and/or patronage capital retirement. Any Other
Withdrawals must be accompanied by a Wolverine Board of Directors’ Resolution declaring the
purpose and the amount.

                                           Definitions

As used in this Rate Schedule No. 4, the following terms have the meanings specified below:

Actual Cost – the cost recorded by Wolverine after the receipt of an invoice during the Rate
Year (N) that is reported on its FERC Form 1.

Actual Revenue – the revenue received and recorded by Wolverine after issuance of an invoice
during the Rate Year (N) that is reported on its FERC Form 1.

Ancillary Services – services that are necessary to support Capacity and the transmission of
Energy from resources to delivery points while maintaining reliable operation of the transmission
system in accordance with Good Utility Practice.

Annual Budget – Wolverine’s projection produced no later than September 30 prior to the

Annual Budget True-up – the mechanism to return or collect from the D Members the actual

included in the Annual Budget.

Annual Coincident Peak – the highest single hourly Demand Metered during a given calendar

Annual Demand Response Resource (ADRR) – Demand Response Resource capable of
performing every month of the year.

Annual Energy Sales – the total amount of Energy Metered during a given calendar year for all
D Members, expressed in MWh.

Annual Forecast – Wolverine’s projection produced no later than September 30 prior to the
immediately upcoming Rate Year (N) of all Variable Costs and Variable Revenue to be
recovered and provided during the Rate Year (N).

Annual Peak Capacity Resource (APCR) – a resource capable of meeting or reducing Metered
Load however, seasonal availability, performance capability, or efficiency limits regular output
to fewer than 12 months per year. For units fired by fossil fuel this category shall include those
units with heat rates of 12,000 BTU/kWh and higher. SDRR are included in this category.

of an APCR.

Variable Cost incurred in the production of Energy by Resources whose costs are recovered in

Baseload Resource – a resource that generally is operating at a minimum level of output (MW)

Base Fixed Costs – the total annual Direct Fixed Cost for all resources that are included in the
Baseload Resource category, Wolverine-owned Renewable Resources, and all other owned

Billing Month – the month for which the current bill is being issued. For example, January’s bill

Capacity – the maximum ability to produce or avoid the consumption of electricity, generally

generation or Demand Response resources.

Commercial Fiber – supplemental fiber optic cables installed with Wolverine’s Utility Fiber

included as part of Wolverine’s Shared Excluded Facilities.

Committed Fixed Costs – costs that are unavoidable as Wolverine is obligated by ownership or
contract to pay regardless of Wolverine operations, D Member Load, or dispatch of the asset.
Committed Fixed Costs include, but are not limited to, interest, depreciation, property tax, and
Capacity PPAs.

Committed Variable Costs –costs that are unavoidable as Wolverine is obligated, by ownership
or contract, to pay regardless of Wolverine operations, D Member Load, or performance of the

renewables, fuel, and fuel transportation.

Current Month – the month in which the bill is being issued. For example, if December is the
Billing Month, January is generally the month in which the bill is issued – January is the Current
Month.

Day-Ahead Locational Marginal Pricing (DA LMP) – an inclusive price for Energy,
congestion, and losses calculated for each hour one day in advance of delivery for a specific
commercial pricing node within a given RTO and represented in $/MWh.

Demand – the maximum integrated hourly sum of Load occurring over a specified period, such
as an hour, day, month, season, or year, expressed in MWs.

Demand Response – the ability to reduce Demand via distributed generation or command of
other distributed devices on the distribution system.

Demand Response Credit – reduction in the monthly bill provided to the D Member for the
ability of the D Member to control and reduce Demand via D Member Demand Response,
qualifications further described herein.

Direct Fixed Costs – costs associated with investing, maintaining, and owning Wolverine’s
power plants, transmission facilities, distribution substations, or other facilities for the benefit of
D Members. These costs include, but are not limited to, depreciation, interest, property tax,

unit(s).

D Member Annual Peak Cost Share –proportion of the Individual D Member Average Annual

Monthly Coincident Peak – the highest single hourly Demand Metered in a given month for all

Monthly Peak Capacity Resource (MPCR) – a resource capable of meeting or reducing

For units fired by fossil fuel this category shall include those units with heat rates between 8,000
BTU/kWh and 11,999 BTU/kWh. Additionally, Capacity PPAs for all non-Baseload and ADRR
resources shall be included in this category.

Monthly Peak Fixed Costs – the total annual Direct Fixed Costs for all resources that are

MPCR Energy Credit – Variable Revenue from the Metered Energy sales minus Variable Cost

N – represents a particular calendar year for which the rate is effective.

Owned Resources – power plants owned or contracted (when for a specific resource(s)), by

PJM –PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., or successor RTO.

Planning Year – the period of time from June 1st of one year to May 31st of the following year

Power Delivery Cost –net of the collective costs and revenues received associated with serving
Load within RTOs, generally referenced as Schedules under the applicable RTO Tariffs, for
items associated with the transmission, transformation, and management of the system including,
 Wolverine Power Supply Cooperative, Inc.                                             Page 9 of 40

but not limited to, transmission and Ancillary Services. The revenues included shall be those and
only those provided for service of Load, as described further within.

Power Delivery Peak – the highest hourly Metered Demand for the individual D Member, plus

Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) – a contractual arrangement between two parties for the
purchase and sale of Energy, capacity, ancillary services, or some combination thereof.

Rate Year – calendar years N, N-x, or N+x.

Real-time Locational Marginal Pricing (RT LMP) – a price inclusive of Energy, congestion,
and losses, generally set in 5-minute intervals and settled hourly during the operating day at a
specific commercial pricing node within a given RTO.

Real-time Energy Purchase – in the course of business Wolverine will require energy
purchases during the operating day, including, but not limited to; under forecasting D Member

Real-time Energy Sales – in the course of business Wolverine will sell energy during the
operating day, including, but not limited to; over forecasting D Member Load in the Day-Ahead
market and deviations from cleared Day-Ahead generation schedules.

RTO –Regional Transmission Organization, as defined by FERC, in which Wolverine
participates (or subsequently participates), including but not limited to MISO and PJM.
 Wolverine Power Supply Cooperative, Inc.                                            Page 10 of 40

Renewable PPA – an agreement for the purchase by Wolverine of attributes produced by a
Renewable Resource, including but not limited to: Energy, renewable energy credits, Capacity,

Renewable Resource – generation that produces energy from sources that are naturally

Renewable Energy Cost – if positive, this is the amount charged, or, if negative, credited, to D
Members determined by subtracting the cost of Wolverine’s Renewable PPA Commitments from
the DA LMP or RT LMP at the respective commercial pricing node at which each Renewable
PPA is settled, as determined in the respective contract or confirmation.

Resolution – formal authorization of an action adopted by the Wolverine Board of Directors.

Seasonal Demand Response Resource (SDRR) – Demand Response capable of performing in

Total Average Annual Coincident Peak – the sum of all D Member non-C&I Annual
Coincident Peaks from the three previously completed Rate Years (N-2, N-3, N-4) divided by
three (3).

Total Average Energy Sales – the sum of Annual Energy Sales to all D Members from the three
previously completed Rate Years (N-2, N-3, N-4) divided by three (3).

Peaks from every month during the three previously completed Rate Years (N-2, N-3, N-4)

Utility Fiber – fiber optic cables installed to provide SCADA communications to rural electrical
stations, create secure private networks to enhance cyber-security, and other Wolverine utility

Variable Costs – costs that are incurred based on the amount of consumption, production,
operation, or other function that change over a short period of time, typically hourly, daily, or
monthly. These costs include, but are not limited to, fuel, PPAs, RTO market purchases, and
variable operations and maintenance costs. Examples of variable costs are natural gas, Dynamic
Energy, and Power Delivery Costs.

Rate Schedule No. 4, Version 54.0.0


Variable Revenue – revenues received that are incurred based on the amount of production,
operation, or other function that change over a short period of time, typically hourly, daily, or
monthly. These revenues include, but are not limited to, Metered Energy sales from generation
Resources to RTOs, PPA energy sales to non-D Members, and Energy Revenue from MBR
contracts with D Members.

Variable Cost True Up – the mechanism to return over-collected amounts to or collect under-
collected amounts from the D Members as actual costs and revenues received vary from what
was billed throughout the applicable rate year (N). Examples include market resettlement
impacting Power Delivery Costs, Real-time Energy Purchases and Sales, or other unknown
Variable Costs or Revenues at the time of billing.

Variable Revenue True Up – the mechanism to return under-credited amounts to or collect
over-credited amounts from the D Members as actual costs and revenues received vary from
what was billed throughout the applicable rate year (N). Examples include market resettlement
impacting Power Delivery Costs, Real-time Energy Purchases and Sales, or other unknown
Variable Costs or Revenues at the time of billing.

Wholesale Power Contract – means the contract for Wolverine providing wholesale electric
sales and transmission service to D Members that is accepted for filing by FERC, as such
contract may be amended from time to time.

Wolverine –Wolverine Power Supply Cooperative, Inc.

Rate Schedule No. 4, Version 54.0.0



                                 General Terms and Conditions


   Availability: Service under this Rate Schedule No. 4 is available to the D Members for
    resale by such Members.

   Requirements to Qualify for Rates: All rates under this Rate Schedule No. 4 apply to each
    D Member, unless specific qualification is otherwise identified with respect to a particular
    rate.

   Billing and Payment Terms: Billing and payment shall be rendered in accordance with the
    requirements set forth in the Wholesale Power Contracts.

   Late Payments: In addition to other remedies that may be available as set forth in the
    Wholesale Power Contracts, Wolverine may charge interest on late payments. If a bill is not
    paid by its due date, interest costs at the prime rate (as published in the Wall Street Journal)
    plus 2% per annum shall accrue from the due date of the bill to the date payment is received
    by Wolverine.

   Payment Mechanism: Bills shall be paid via electronic means (such as a wire transfer or
    Automated Clearing House payment).
 Wolverine Power Supply Cooperative, Inc.                                           Page 13 of 40
Rate Schedule No. 4, Version 54.0.0


                          Fixed Cost Charges and Revenue Credits
Overview

Each month Wolverine will assess and provide the following formula Costs and revenue credits
in accordance with the Fixed Cost Distribution to recover its Fixed Costs within three categories
(Base, Annual Peak, and Monthly Peak). When annualized, collectively these costs and credits
make -up the Annual Fixed Costs:

   1.   Base Fixed Costs
   2.   Base Fixed Revenue Credits
   3.   Margin Components
   4.   Annual Peak Fixed Costs
   5.   Annual Peak Fixed Revenue Credits
   6.   Monthly Peak Fixed Costs
   7.   Monthly Peak Fixed Revenue Credits

All costs and credits shown above are initially based on the Annual Budget, after the conclusion
of the Rate Year (N) all of these costs and credits are subject to the Annual Budget True-up, as
described below.

Base Fixed Costs

The Base Fixed Costs shall be charged on the Current Month’s bill and are based on the Billing
Month’s share of the Base Fixed Costs as included in the Annual Budget and the Annual Budget
True-up. The Billing Month’s share of the Base Fixed Costs shall be determined by taking the
total Base Fixed Costs as calculated for the Annual Budget and the Annual Budget True-up for
Base Fixed Costs from Rate Year (N-1) less Base Fixed Costs and Annual Budget True-up for
Base Fixed Cost from Rate Year (N-1) allocated to load charged under the C&I Rate and then
multiplied by Fixed Cost Distribution and by D Member Base Fixed Cost Share.

Base Fixed Costs ($) = [total Base Fixed Costs included in Annual Budget for Rate Year (N) +
total Annual Budget True-up for Base Fixed Costs for Rate Year (N-1) – Base Fixed Costs and
Annual Budget True-up for Base Fixed Cost from Rate Year (N-1) allocated to load charged
under the C&I Rate] * [Fixed Cost Distribution] * [D Member Base Fixed Cost Share]

Base Fixed Revenue Credit

The Base Fixed Revenue Credit shall be credited on the Current Month’s bill, is based on the
Billing Month’s share of the Base Fixed Revenue Credit earned for sales of Capacity and
Ancillary Services, and is determined by calculating the total revenue received from the sales of
Capacity and Ancillary Services from Base Resources as calculated for the Annual Budget for
the applicable Rate Year (N) less Base Fixed Revenue Credit and allocated to load charged under
 Wolverine Power Supply Cooperative, Inc.                                            Page 14 of 40
Rate Schedule No. 4, Version 54.0.0


the C&I Rate and then multiplied by the Fixed Cost Distribution and then multiplied by the D
Member Base Fixed Cost Share.

Base Fixed Revenue Credit ($) = [sum Base Fixed Revenue Credits included in Annual Budget
for Rate Year (N) – Base Fixed Revenue Credits allocated to load charged under the C&I Rate] *
[Fixed Cost Distribution] * [D Member Base Fixed Cost Share]

Margin Components

Margin shall be included in the Annual Budget as part of the Base Fixed Costs and recovered as
part of the Billing Month’s share of the Base Fixed Costs, as shown immediately above. Margin
shall be earned in the following two ways:

       1. Return on Interest Expense

       Return on Interest Expense, which is the total of all interest expense included in the Base,
       Monthly Peak, and Annual Peak Fixed Cost categories as part of the Annual Budget for
       the Applicable Rate Year (N) and multiplied by 70%. (e.g. 1.70x TIER)

       Return on Interest Expense ($) = [sum of interest expense included in the Base, Monthly
       Peak, and Annual Peak Fixed Costs] * 70%

       2. Unbudgeted Fixed Revenue

       Unbudgeted Fixed Revenue – If Wolverine earns Fixed Revenue in any of the Base,
       Monthly Peak, or Annual Peak categories in excess of what is included in the Annual
       Budget for the applicable Rate Year (N) the difference between the sum of actual Fixed
       Revenue received during the Rate Year and the total Annual Budget of all Fixed Revenue
       Credits provided shall result in margin for the applicable Rate Year (N).

       Unbudgeted Fixed Revenue ($) = sum of actual Fixed Base, Monthly Peak, and Annual
       Peak Revenue received during the Rate Year (N) – total Annual Budget Fixed Revenue
       Credits for the applicable Rate Year (N)

Annual Peak Fixed Costs

The Annual Peak Fixed Costs shall be charged on the Current Month’s bill, are based on the

throughout the life of the MDR. The cost for installation and maintenance of the meter shall be
borne solely by the D Member receiving the benefit of the MDR. Wolverine must either install
the meter or approve of the meter being installed and must have the ability to receive MDR
output interval data, at least hourly.

MDR Cost Recovery

Wolverine will recover the cost for MDR depending on the method under which the MDR is
procured – either by Wolverine ownership or contract, as mutually agreed between the D
Member making the MDR request and Wolverine.

Wolverine-Owned MDR Cost Recovery

Wolverine recovers MDR costs in two categories: maintenance and investment.

MDR Maintenance Cost

Wolverine shall bill participating D Member(s) for all direct operations and maintenance costs
incurred to operate and maintain the asset. These charges shall be billed to the participating D
Member(s) on the Current Month’s bill for all operations and maintenance costs incurred during
the Billing Month.

MDR Ownership Costs

Annual MDR Ownership Costs

The Annual MDR Ownership Cost is determined annually on an MDR by MDR basis for each
MDR based on the sum of actual depreciation, interest expense, property taxes, and all other
direct and indirect costs incurred by Wolverine on behalf of the member for the investment,
ownership, operation, maintenance, decommissioning or termination of the MDR, excluding any
costs included in and collected under MDR Maintenance Costs. With respect solely to then
known or reasonably anticipated costs prior to commencement of construction or execution of a
contractual resource, Wolverine shall project these costs and receive acceptance from the
participating D Member(s) in writing, recognizing that the D Member is obligated to pay actual
costs incurred as reconciled at the conclusion of the project.

Annual MDR Ownership Cost ($) = sum of the [depreciation, interest expense, property taxes,
and any other direct and indirect cost incurred due to investment and on-going ownership as
described above].

Monthly MDR Ownership Cost

Each month after commercial operation Wolverine shall bill the Annual MDR Ownership Cost
($) multiplied by 1/12.

Monthly MDR Ownership Cost ($) = Annual MDR Ownership Cost ($) * 1/12

Retirement of Wolverine-Owned MDR

If at any time a D Member notifies Wolverine in writing that an MDR, that Wolverine owns on
the D Member’s behalf, is no longer needed for any reason, Wolverine shall de-energize that
MDR as soon as practicable.

If the MDR has not been fully depreciated when it is de-energized, within twelve (12) months of
de-energization, Wolverine shall bill the D Member for the remaining net book value of the de-
energized MDR less any salvage value that Wolverine obtains from selling reusable equipment.

Contract MDR Cost Recovery

Contract MDR Cost

Each full Current Month after the commercial operation date of the MDR, Wolverine shall bill
the D Member(s) for Wolverine’s Estimated Costs for the MDR based on the applicable contract
costs. Additionally, previous Billing Month’s Estimated Costs will be trued-up with Actual
Costs. This true-up will be added to the monthly bill by adding the difference of the billed
Estimated Contract MDR Cost and Actual Contract MDR Cost.

Contract MDR Cost ($) = [Estimated Contract MDR cost] + [billed Estimated Contract MDR
cost from previous Billing Month – Actual Contract MDR cost from previous Billing Month]

Retirement of Contract MDR

Under no circumstance may the participating D Member be released of an on-going MDR
contractual obligation and related costs. If the participating D Member desires to end the
obligation earlier than the expiration date, Wolverine shall use best efforts to negotiate an early
termination on its behalf.

MDR Cost Avoidance and Credit Capture

An MDR enables the participating D Member to avoid two charges under this Rate Schedule:

Dynamic Energy Cost – the MWh production of the MDR reduces the amount of Energy
required to serve the participating D Member.

Power Delivery Cost – output MW from the MDR during Power Delivery Peak Hours reduces
the Demand requirements for the participating D Member.

An MDR may qualify to receive the Demand Response Credit under this Rate Schedule.

MDR Output Add Back

To ensure equitable treatment the participating D Member’s contribution toward any Committed
Fixed Costs and Committed Variable Costs or receipt of Fixed or Variable Credits, production
from the MDR facility shall be added back to Energy sales, Monthly Coincident Peaks, and
Annual Coincident Peaks in the following manner:

Energy sales – all Metered Energy production shall be added to the participating D Member’s
Energy consumption used to determine D Member share of Committed Fixed Costs and
Committed Variable Costs and Fixed and Variable Costs and Credits.

Monthly Coincident Peak – if the MDR was operating during the Monthly Coincident Peak, the
hourly Metered output of the MDR shall be added back to the participating D Member Demand
for that applicable hour used to determine D Member share of Committed Fixed Costs and
Committed Variable Costs and Fixed and Variable Credits.

Annual Coincident Peak – if the MDR was operating during the Annual Coincident Peak, the
hourly Metered output of the MDR shall be added back to the participating D Member Demand
for that applicable hour used to determine D Member share of Committed Fixed Costs and
Committed Variable Costs and Fixed and Variable Credits.

                                  Member Directed Programs

Wolverine’s D Members may direct Wolverine to establish new programs to spur rural economic

the D Members and must receive authorization via Resolution of the Wolverine Board of

Programs

Economic Development

the health, resilience, and vibrance of the rural communities they serve.

Beneficial Electrification

RTO Market Programs

D Member Eligibility

Authorization

                                 Distribution Substation Rate

Overview

Each D Member shall be billed for distribution substations that Wolverine owns and that benefit
the D Member. Each individual D Member shall be responsible for its costs associated with
distribution substations. Wolverine has two monthly cost categories for distribution substations,
with different billing units for each cost, Distribution Substation Maintenance and Distribution
Substation Investment.

When D Members share a particular substation, both monthly substation costs categories shall be
allocated to the sharing D Member on the basis of the percentage contribution of each D Member
to the Annual Coincident Peak Demand at that shared distribution substation for the most
recently completed Rate Year (N-2).

Distribution Substation Maintenance (DSM) Cost

Wolverine shall annually update the DSM Cost based on an average cost of service of the three
previously complete Rate Years (N-2, N-3, N-4). This is determined by dividing the (a) total
annual Direct and allocated operations and maintenance expenses incurred by Wolverine for
Rate Years (N-2, N-3, N-4) for distribution divided by (b) three (3).

Annual DSM Cost for Rate Year (N) = [sum annual direct operations and maintenance expenses
from three (3) previously completed Rate Years (N-2, N-3, N-4)] /three (3)

DSM Monthly Billing

Monthly DSM Cost for Rate Year (N) = Annual DSM Cost for Rate Year (N)/ [sum the number
of distribution substations in service at the end of the previously completed Rate Year (N-
1)]/twelve (12)

Each month during the Rate Year (N) Wolverine shall bill each D Member the Monthly DSM
Cost multiplied by the number of distribution substations serving that particular D Member.

DSM Monthly ($) = Monthly DSM Cost * number of distribution substations serving D Member

Distribution Substation Investment (DSI) Cost

The Annual DSI Cost is determined by the sum of depreciation, interest, property taxes, and
return on substation investment serving the D Members and expressed as an annual fixed charge
rate carrying cost as a percentage basis. Wolverine shall determine the applicable DSI Cost
components based on the sum of each of the respective categories: average depreciation rate,
average interest rate, average property tax rate, and return on interest expense related to
substation investment, where Gross Book Value is reduced for the portion of the distribution

substation upgrades required for the installation and operation of generation facilities
interconnected to the transmission system.

Annual DSI Cost (%) = average depreciation (%) + average interest rate (%) + average property
tax rate (%) + return on interest expense related to distribution substation investment (%)

The Monthly DSI Cost shall be charged on the Current Month’s bill and is based on the Billing

DSI Monthly ($) = Annual DSI Cost (%) * 1/12 * [sum Gross Book Value of the distribution
substations, for all distribution substations serving D Member, on the last day of the month prior

Billing is set to occur.. Upon completion of construction, and after the receipt of the final
construction costs and payment from D Member, Wolverine will net the construction cost and
prepayment on its books resulting in zero ($0) investment cost subject to the DSI Monthly
Billing for the new substation. Any pPrepaid substation(s) or prepaid substation upgrades paid by

in aid to construction.

Retirement of Substations

substations is no longer needed for any reason, Wolverine shall de-energize that substation as
soon as practicable.

If the substation has not been fully depreciated when it is de-energized, within twelve (12)
months of de-energization, Wolverine shall bill the D Member for the remaining net book value
of the de-energized substation less any salvage value that Wolverine obtains from selling
reusable equipment in the substation.

                                    Excluded Facilities Rate

Overview

Wolverine owns two types of transmission facilities: facilities that qualify for rate recovery
through an RTO (referred to as “included” facilities) and other transmission facilities
(“excluded” facilities). Some of Wolverine’s excluded facilities serve all of the D Members;
these facilities are called “Shared Excluded Facilities (SEF).” The remainder of Wolverine’s
excluded facilities serve one or more D Members, but not all of them; these are called
“Dedicated Excluded Facilities (DEF).”

Excluded Facilities Cost

The annual Excluded Facilities Cost is determined by the sum of depreciation, interest, property
taxes, return on interest, and average maintenance cost of all Excluded Facilities as a percentage
of Gross Book Value, expressed as an annual fixed charge rate reflected as percentage basis.
Wolverine shall determine the applicable Excluded Facilities Cost components based on the sum
of each of the respective categories: average depreciation rate, average interest rate, average
property tax rate, return on interest expense, and average direct maintenance cost.

Annual Excluded Facilities Cost (%) = sum of the [average depreciation (%), average interest
rate (%), average property tax rate (%), return on interest expense (%), and average direct
maintenance cost (%)]

DEF Monthly Billing

Each month during the Rate Year (N) Wolverine shall bill the Annual Excluded Facilities Cost
multiplied by 1/12 multiplied by the sum of the Gross Book Value of the DEF serving the
particular D Member as of the final day of the month prior to the applicable Billing Month
multiplied by the D Member DEF Share.

DEF Monthly ($) = Annual Excluded Facilities Cost (%) * 1/12 * [sum Gross Book Value of all
DEF facilities serving D Member, on the last day of the month prior to the Billing Month]

Prepayment for DEF

D Members may prepay for a new DEF in its entirety. For each prepaid DEF, Wolverine shall
require prepayment for the estimated cost of construction of the new DEF (including
construction financing cost inured to the project) before the start of construction and final
payment (or credit) of construction cost prior to energizing of the new DEF. The estimated
prepayment amount will be made in full prior to the commencement of the new substation, or at
option of the D Member instigating construction, in two installments. If the D Member chooses
to make installment payments, 70% of the estimated cost of construction will be due before the

start of construction and 30% of the estimated cost will be due at the mid-point of the
construction schedule; final payment (or credit) of the construction cost is due prior to energizing
of the new DEF. Upon completion of construction, and after the receipt of the final construction
costs, Wolverine will net the construction cost and prepayment on its books resulting in zero ($0)
investment cost subject to the DEF Monthly Billing for the new substation. DEF Prepayment
does not exempt the contributing D Member(s) from any direct maintenance cost of the facility.
Any direct maintenance costs incurred by Wolverine will be billed directly to the contributing D
Member(s) on a pro rata basis.

Retirement of DEF

If at any time the D Member(s) notifies Wolverine in writing that one of its particular DEF is no
longer needed for any reason, Wolverine shall de-commission that DEF as soon as practicable.

If the DEF has not been fully depreciated when it is de-energized, within twelve (12) months of
de-commissioned, Wolverine shall bill the D Member(s) for the remaining net book value of the
de-energized DEF less any salvage value that Wolverine obtains from selling reusable equipment
from the DEF.

Shared Excluded Facilities (SEF)

SEF Share

All D Member’s share in the SEF Cost based on its respective Annual Coincident Peak divided
by the sum total Annual Coincident Peaks for all D Members from the most recently completed
Rate Year (N-1), expressed as a percentage.

SEF Monthly Billing

Each month during the Rate Year (N) Wolverine shall bill of the Annual Excluded Facilities
Cost multiplied by 1/12 multiplied by the sum of the Gross Book Value of the SEF serving the
particular D Member as of the final day of the month prior to the applicable Billing Month
multiplied by the D Member SEF Share.

SEF Monthly ($) = Annual Excluded Facilities Cost (%) * 1/12 * [sum Gross Book Value of the
SEF serving D Members, on the last day of the month prior to the Billing Month] * D Member
SEF Share

Credits for Excluded Facilities

If Wolverine receives revenue directly from D Members for use of SEF or non-D Members for
use of any Excluded Facility, DEF or SEF, the revenue shall be credited to the applicable
Excluded Facility, DEF or SEF.

                                 Retail Access Standby Rate

Overview

Michigan law permits retail electric cooperative Member-Consumers with Loads of more than
1 MW to obtain electric power from an Alternative Electric Supplier (“AES”) instead of from
their electric cooperative. When a Member-Consumer chooses to obtain its power from an AES,
and that AES fails to provide power to the Member-Consumer, the D Member may permit that
Member-Consumer to obtain standby electric power from the D Member on a best efforts-basis.
If the D Member permits such an arrangement, Wolverine will provide wholesale standby
electric power to its D Member at the prices shown in this Rate Schedule, and the D Member
will then provide standby service to the Member-Consumer pursuant to the D Member’s retail
tariffs. Wolverine is not required to build or purchase new Capacity or interrupt firm service
customers to provide wholesale standby service under this rate schedule. No credits apply under
this Standby Rate.

For Member-Consumers receiving standby service, Wolverine will bill the D Member each
month for the Standby Variable Costs and Standby Fixed costs, both as described below.

Standby Variable Cost

The Standby Variable Cost shall be the highest of the following Costs for the Member-
Consumer requiring standby service, for each hour when service was provided during any
month:

       1. The total actual monthly average, expressed in $/MWh, of all Variable Costs and
          excluding Variable Credits (both of which are defined elsewhere in this Rate
          Schedule No. 4), plus ten (10) percent;
       2. Wolverine’s highest incremental cost of any generation or purchases of power during
          all hours served, plus ten (10) percent, plus applicable transmission Costs and
          ancillary service Costs; and
       3. The highest locational marginal price applicable to Wolverine for all hours served,
          plus ten (10) percent, plus applicable transmission Costs and ancillary service Costs.

Standby Fixed Cost

The Standby Fixed Cost shall be of the hourly average, expressed in $/MWh, of all Wolverine’s
Fixed Costs, plus ten (10) percent, for the highest single hourly Metered Demand of the
Member-Consumer during the entire period the standby service was required.
 Wolverine Power Supply Cooperative, Inc.                                           Page 39 of 40
Rate Schedule No. 4, Version 54.0.0


                     True-UpRate Stabilization Rider for 2019 and 2020


Rate Target

Beginning with Rate Year, 2027, and for each Rate Year thereafter, Wolverine shall set a Rate
Target for its Total Power Supply and Delivery Rate. For Rate Year 2027 the Rate Target is
established by the Wolverine Board of Directors in accordance with the Resolution authorizing
this Rate Stabilization Rider. For each subsequent Rate Year, starting with Rate Year 2028, the
Wolverine Board of Directors shall establish the Rate Target to align with the Annual Forecast
deadline.

Total Power Supply and Delivery Rate shall be defined as Wolverine’s total cost of energy,
capacity, and power delivery to supply its D Members under this Rate Schedule. Total Power
Supply Rate is calculated as follows:

Total Power Supply and Delivery Rate ($/MWh) = [Fixed Cost Charges and Revenue Credits +
Variable Costs and Revenues] / Annual Energy Sales for the applicable Rate Year

Rate Stabilization Fund

At the end of each Billing Month Wolverine shall manage its Total Power Supply and Delivery
Rate to achieve the Rate Target. The Rate Stabilization Fund shall be established to achieve the
Rate Target for the benefit of D Members. At the end of each Billing Month, Wolverine shall
determine whether the funds will be deposited to or withdrawn from the Rate Stabilization Fund
as follows:

Rate Stabilization Fund Deposit/(Withdrawal) ($) = [Rate Target ($/MWh) – Total Power Supply
and Delivery Rate ($/MWh) for the applicable Billing Month] * Energy Sales for the applicable
Billing Month

If the results of the calculation above are positive, the amount shall be deposited as a Rate
Stabilization Fund Deposit and held for future use by Wolverine to achieve the Rate Target or for
other purposes as defined herein.

If the results of the calculation above are negative, the amount shall be withdrawn as a Rate
Stabilization Fund Withdrawal to be applied as Variable Revenue, to achieve the Rate Target.

Insufficient Stabilization Fund Balance

If a Rate Stabilization Fund Withdrawal is required because the Rate Target was not achieved
and the then-current balance of the fund is insufficient to achieve the Rate Target, the
 Wolverine Power Supply Cooperative, Inc.                                            Page 40 of 40
Rate Schedule No. 4, Version 54.0.0


Stabilization Fund Withdrawal shall be drawn to zero to reduce the Total Power Supply and
Delivery Rate as close to the Target Rate as possible.

Other Withdrawals

At the discretion of the Wolverine Board of Directors, funds may be withdrawn from the Rate
Stabilization Fund for power supply investment and/or patronage capital retirement. Any Other
Withdrawals must be accompanied by a Wolverine Board of Directors’ Resolution declaring the
purpose and amount.

To facilitate the transition of each D Member to a new rate design, and to reconcile any then
remaining balances in D Member accounts as of the effective date of the revised Rate Schedule,
this Rider implements a revised True-Up mechanism as applied in this Rate Schedule to
Wolverine’s actual costs in 2019 and 2020. This Rider revises the time period to collect the
True-Up but does not change the formulas used in determining the True-Up.
In lieu of settling the True-Up of energy and demand costs from two years earlier (N-2),
Wolverine will net the immediately prior two years of costs applicable to this Rate Schedule
(2019 & 2020) and settle both True-Ups at one time. If the combined costs result in an:
   A. Under-collection less than $1 million Wolverine shall collect lump sum settlements.
   B. Under-collection greater than $1 million Wolverine shall collect from each D Member
      one-twelfth (1/12) true-up of such amount in each D Member’s monthly invoice issued in
      2021.
   C. Over-collection Wolverine shall pay lump sum settlements.
The initial payment or collection shall be issued on the first D Member bill after Wolverine has
completed its preliminary close of the 2020 Fiscal Year. The final True-Up payment or
collection for the 2019 and 2020 rate years shall be determined after Wolverine has completed
the 2020 FERC Form 1. Any differences from the preliminary 2020 close shall be settled in
accordance with the outline above.

                        Wolverine Power Supply Cooperative, Inc.

                                     RESOLUTION 2026-10

        WHEREAS, Wolverine Power Supply Cooperative, Inc. ("Wolverine") currently has approved
rates on file with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission ("FERC") in Wolverine Power Supply
Cooperative, Inc., FERC Rate Schedule No. 4, Version 4.0.0 ("Wholesale Rate Schedule") in Docket
No. ER21-66;

        WHEREAS, Cherryland Electric Cooperative, Great Lakes Energy Cooperative, HomeWorks Tri­
County Electric Cooperative, Presque Isle Gas & Electric Co-op, and Midwest Energy & Communications
purchase wholesale electric power from Wolverine pursuant to an Amended and Restated Wholesale Power
Contract with an accepted and effective date of May 8, 2020 ("2020 Contract") in Docket No. ER20- l 206,
as well as Thumb Electric Cooperative with an accepted and effective date of January 1, 2025 ("2025
Contract") in Docket No. ER25-265; and these six companies comprise Wolverine's "Distribution
Cooperative Member-Owners";

         WHEREAS, Section 4(b) of the 2020 Contract and the 2025 Contract with the Distribution
Cooperative Member-Owners provides that Wolverine is entitled to periodically review and revise the rates
for electric power furnished under the Wholesale Rate Schedule;

       WHEREAS, Wolverine is seeking to update its present rates which became effective on January 1,
2027 to establish a methodology and mechanism to provide Member rate stability, predictability,
competitiveness, and financial flexibility; and

        WHEREAS, Wolverine has reviewed and discussed the proposed Rate Stabilization Mechanism
and its operation within Wolverine's current rate design with the Wolverine Board of Directors and has
demonstrated that the proposed changes wi11, among other things, continue to accurately reflect Wolverine's
actual costs and revenues both now and in future years, while providing ongoing competitiveness,
predictability, stability, and flexibility.

       NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS RESOLVED, that the Wolverine Board of Directors hereby
approves the revised Wholesale Rate Schedule, as proposed by Wolverine management, to be filed with
FERC, for a target effective date of January I, 2027; and

        BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Board of Directors authorizes Wolverine and its
authorized representatives to take any actions necessary to carry out this Resolution and make any
revisions to the revised Wholesale Rate Schedule filing deemed necessary to effectuate this resolution.
